strategy_name: Scheduled-event volatility risk rule (news stop-outs)
mechanism: volatility and spread expansion before scheduled announcements produce wild whipsaws that hit stops regardless of the eventual direction
setup_summary: Before a scheduled high-impact release (FX: NFP, FOMC, CPI, trade balance, retail sales; crypto analog: CPI/FOMC), either widen the stop by the expected spread-expansion distance (book suggests 5-10 pips for higher TF stops), or reduce position size so the widened stop preserves the originally intended loss, or close the position before the release. Never leave a tight stop near price when an announcement is imminent.
trigger_invalidation: Applies only when a high-impact release is scheduled within the holding period; no adjustment needed when no announcement is pending over the trade horizon.
risk_geometry: Stop width scaled by expected spread widening; position sized so loss-at-widened-stop equals the intended loss (stop_distance_atr variant with an event premium).
quote: The volatility jumps before important anouncements and the drastic movements can hit the stop-losses, resulting in a lost trade and investment.
chapter_anchor: Section 03, When & why do spreads tighten / How to trade during the news events
notes: BTCUSDT 1h produces violent wicks around US CPI and FOMC releases; a deterministic event-calendar stop-widening rule is directly implementable in RiskGate without new data streams (the calendar is knowable in advance). The book warns the widened spread 'will get you' even if the announcement favors you, because price whipsaws a few pips before taking direction.
book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

strategy_name: SafeZone noise-based stop (Average Penetration x coefficient)
mechanism: bar-to-bar penetration of prior extremes measures current market noise; placing the stop one coefficient-of-noise beyond recent extremes keeps it out of noise without using ATR or swing points
setup_summary: Stop placement rule: in an uptrend, market noise = the extent today's low extends below yesterday's low (Downside Penetration); stop = lows − (Average Downside Penetration over the lookback period x coefficient). In a downtrend, stop = highs + (Average Upside Penetration x coefficient). Pure noise measurement — no ATR, no swing point.
trigger_invalidation: Applies to any open position: stop is hit -> exit. If the trend flips, switch which penetration side (upside vs downside) is used for stops.
risk_geometry: Entry per the trend method; stop = Average Downside Penetration x coefficient below lows (long) or Average Upside Penetration x coefficient above highs (short); lookback window and coefficient are the only parameters; stop is sized to clear recent noise.
quote: Market noise is the extent by which today's extreme price extends outside yesterday's extreme... multiply Average Downside Penetration by the coefficient and subtract it from the lows to place stops in uptrends.
chapter_anchor: Answer 61; also BVF exit answer (buy orders 'as many points below the EMA as the average depth of past penetrations')
notes: Strong candidate for a V8 stop-placement rule alongside atr_stop: uses bar-to-bar extreme penetration, robust in 24/7 markets with no gaps. Complements the V8 dead-thesis exit: SafeZone handles normal noise stops, trend-flip handles thesis invalidation.
book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

strategy_name: Volatility/fear index as contrarian indicator
mechanism: fear-extreme contrarian: when a fear/volatility index (VIX; perp analog: DVOL/BVOL or funding-spike gauge) reaches an extreme, the crowd is positioned one way and the underlying tends to reverse rather than continue
setup_summary: When the fear index registers an extreme (very high = capitulation-fear, very low = complacency), fade the extreme: high-fear readings bias LONG reversal, low-fear/extreme-complacency readings bias SHORT. Falsifiable as a threshold regime filter on the fear gauge.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fear gauge crosses an extreme threshold. Invalidation: fear stays/extends (no reversion within N bars) or underlying makes a new extreme in the fear direction.
risk_geometry: Regime/filter, not a standalone entry: gates direction admission; no direct entry/stop geometry from the book.
quote: VIX index, 109-115; as contrarian indicator, 109; herding behavior, 109; risk aversion, 109
chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 109-115 (VIX as fear index and contrarian indicator)
notes: VIX-as-contrarian is an empirically documented claim; perp analog is a crypto vol index (DVOL/BVOL) or funding-rate extreme gauge. Use as a regime filter in the risk-admission path, not an expert.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Stop distance beyond noise; dollar stops over technical stops; risk-budget sizing
mechanism: Stops are a damage-control shield against unpredictable price; stops placed within random fluctuation get 'gunned' and convert profitable entries into losses. Stop distance is the single largest performance variable in a system.
setup_summary: Always use a stop, placed with the broker, located beyond the market's random fluctuation rather than at tight technical levels; size positions so risk per trade is capped (e.g., 5% of a $100k account). Empirical demonstration on one identical S&P day system: a $500 stop lost $41,750 (26% accuracy); the same entries with a $1,500 stop made +$116,880 (56% accuracy); a $6,000 stop made +$269,525 (70% accuracy) but raised the largest losing trade to $5,920.
trigger_invalidation: A stop is mis-placed if routine noise hits it (too tight) or if per-trade risk exceeds the money-management budget (too wide for the account size).
risk_geometry: Entry not specified by the rule (applies to any entry); stop = dollar-based beyond noise (~$800-$1,200 commodities; $1,750-$2,500 S&P) or a key market turning point; a time stop (end of day) may be coupled with the dollar stop; sizing = risk budget / stop distance (at 5% of $100k, a $6,000 stop allows 1 contract while a $1,500 stop allows 2, doubling profit on the same account).
quote: the closer your stop is the more often you will be stopped out ... stops must be beyond-or past-random fluctuations.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 15, 'Comments on Setting Stops' (pp. 240-243); 'Learning How To Lose Money' (pp. 223-224)
notes: Direct input to V8 RiskGate and stop design: stop distance should be derived from noise/ATR, not fixed tight levels — consistent with V8's stop_r/ATR-ref geometry. Crypto specifics: no gaps means wide stops are not gap-through hazards, and high leverage makes the contracts = risk-budget / stop-distance sizing rule essential; dollar stops should be expressed in volatility terms (funding and fees affect stop-and-reverse frequency).
book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

strategy_name: Volatility-scaled stop/target framework (2xATR stop, 3xATR target, -8% cap, RR 1.25-2.0)
mechanism: Correlating per-trade loss tolerance with the instrument's volatility (ATR) bounds risk while allowing reward of 1.5-3x risk; a fixed exact stop price removes discretionary exits.
setup_summary: Every trade requires an exact stop price (not a mental 'area'). Four stop methods: percentage (max -8%, typically -5 to -6%; average loss in the Swing Trade Newsletter ~4.76%), price-pattern (below nearby support / major MA / trendline), ATR (stop at 2xATR, period 14; if 2xATR > 8% from entry the stock is too volatile for a swing trade), parabolic SAR (Wilder price+time stop). Four profit exits: percentage (target 1.5-2.0x the stop distance), price resistance/support, ATR (target 3xATR when stop is 2xATR), and trailing stop (claimed most profitable). Risk/reward minimum: 1.25 with a trailing stop, 2.0+ preferred; scratch any setup that cannot project at least +10% before significant resistance.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — risk layer, applies to every position.
risk_geometry: Stop: max -8% (typ 5-6%) / 2xATR / below structure; target: 1.5-2.0x stop or 3xATR; ATR(14) used both for stops and position sizing.
quote: In most cases, however, due to the relatively short-term nature of these trades, you will want to set a stop-loss no greater than −8 percent on any given trade no matter what you expect to gain from a successful completion of the trade.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Entries and Exits' (pp. 229-237)
notes: Maps directly to V8 risk_geometry (entry/stop_r/target_r/atr_ref): 2xATR stop / 3xATR target is a concrete instantiation of stop_r=2 and target_r=3 with atr_ref=14. The -8% cash-cap translates, under perp leverage, into R-multiple position sizing (risk_percent_sizing). Entry mechanics (pp. 227-229): stop order $0.02-0.05 above prior day's high (longs) / below prior day's low (shorts), gaps handled by limit orders; 'the entry is the least important part of trading.' The RR 1.25/2.0 thresholds are a RiskGate admission rule candidate.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Move-significance noise filter
setup_summary: Classify each bar's move relative to the instrument's usual daily percentage change: unless |move| exceeds its usual daily magnitude the event is treated as noise and no signal weight is attached. Significance is nonlinear in magnitude (a 2% move is roughly 4x as significant as a 1% move), so a 1h BTCUSDT bar whose |return| is a small fraction of typical daily range should be ignored for any directional inference.
trigger_invalidation: A move is deemed signal only when |move| > k * (usual daily % change); thesis invalidated if the filter shows no discrimination versus unfiltered signals on frozen OOS (signal subsets do not out-perform chance), or if the move fully reverts inside the significance window.
risk_geometry: Not a trade; a pre-filter. No entry/stop/target. Feeds volatility-normalized feature or regime gating.
quote: Unless something moves by more than its usual daily percentage change, the event is deemed to be noise.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'The Bloomberg Explanations' (p. 166)
notes: Directly transferable to 24/7 crypto where noise dominates a large share of 1h bars. Candidate input for a volatility-scaled significance gate or feature (volatility-normalized move), complementing V8's existing ATR-scaled risk geometry.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Black-swan crisis harvesting (long convexity)
setup_summary: Portfolio-level strategy of being structurally long tail risk: accept small recurring losses while holding convexity that pays off in market breakdowns ('profiting from the black swans and the breakdown of the system'), the inverse of LTCM's book.
trigger_invalidation: Cannot be expressed in a perps-only book without options/vol instruments; deferred pending venue expansion (crypto options) or a convexity-approximation design.
risk_geometry: Small, repeated premium-like losses; payoff concentrated in rare breakdown events; requires long expiry and no stop that would cut the convex payoff.
quote: I happen to specialize in profiting from the black swans and the breakdown of the system, and make bets against financial economists.
notes: LOW applicability: V8 models Binance USDM perps only, and the canonical expression needs options or vol products. Recorded as a backlog family so the positive-skew preference survives as a screening criterion even though the tradable form is out of venue.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Predetermined falsification stop (black-swan protection)
mechanism: Define in advance which price event falsifies the thesis, and exit mechanically on it; the stop is a predetermined exit point that protects against the rare event
setup_summary: Before entry, specify the observable event that proves the conjecture wrong; pre-place an exit at that level and honor it mechanically when price reaches it or the thesis is invalidated. It is distinct from profit-taking and is the accepted protection of the surviving traders described in the book ('All the surviving traders I know seem to have done the same').
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: entry taken with a pre-specified falsification level. Invalid: price trades through the stop and the exit is deferred; or the thesis was entered with no falsification level defined at all.
risk_geometry: Entry: any; stop: predetermined exit point ('a stop loss, a predetermined exit point'); target/expiry not specified; exit is thesis-falsification-based and separate from the profit target.
quote: This is called a stop loss, a predetermined exit point, a protection from the black swan. I find it rarely practiced.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7, Pascal's Wager (p. 110)
notes: Directly reinforces V8's distinction between the risk_geometry stop and the dead-thesis (still_valid) exit, and the Popperian requirement that a hypothesis state its own refutation conditions. The anti-pattern is Carlos's 'stop losses are for schmucks' denial. Crypto 24/7 + high leverage: no exchange-gap excuse, forced liquidation is the stop you didn't set.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Track-record validity depends on cohort size, not individual skill
mechanism: Observed track records are draws from a cohort; the expected maximum of records depends more on cohort size and volatility than on individual odds, so even incompetent populations produce great-looking records
setup_summary: Methodology: in a fair 50/50 game, 10,000 managers yield ~313 with five consecutive winning years by pure chance; even a cohort of expected losers (45/55) yields ~184 five-year survivors, and 'volatility actually helps bad investment decisions.' The validity of any track record requires knowing the size of the cohort it was drawn from — 10 managers is meaningful, 10,000 is noise. V8 consequence: report the multiplicity of variants/experts screened when evaluating any record, and treat unsolicited/adverse-selected records as near-meaningless.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: track-record-based acceptance of any strategy. Invalid: after cohort-size adjustment the record is consistent with pure chance; no replication outside the original cohort.
risk_geometry: n/a — evaluation methodology.
quote: the expectation of the maximum of track records... depends more on the size of the initial sample, than on the individual odds per manager.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Nobody Has To Be Competent (p. 129-130)
notes: Also grounds the adverse-selection rule: 'the chance of the soliciting party being a spurious survivor is closer to 100%' when the record comes to you. Directly supports V8's registry stages (SCREENING/REPLICATION/SHADOW) and the frozen-OOS evidence gate.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: All-in beats scaling-in in-sample (Schoenberg-Corwin); scaling-in only defensible OOS
mechanism: expected-profit comparison over two possible paths shows averaging-in is never the most profitable entry policy for any fixed transition probability; only time-varying volatility/probability justifies it
setup_summary: For a mean-reversion target F with intermediate level L1 and deeper level L2 (reached with probability p), expected profits show: all-in at L1 dominates if p < p_hat = (F-L1)/(F-L2), all-in at L2 dominates if p > p_hat, and averaging-in (1 unit at L1 + 1 at L2) is never best. Because volatility - hence p - is not constant, scaling-in can still outperform out-of-sample, but it is never optimal in-sample and requires unbounded capital in the linear formulation.
trigger_invalidation: Scaling-in justified only under time-varying volatility/probabilities; otherwise single all-in level dominates.
risk_geometry: Single all-in entry level for mean-reversion entries; avoids the unlimited-capital requirement of linear z-score scaling.
quote: entering or exiting at two or more Bollinger bands is never optimal; that is, you can always find a single entry/exit level that will generate a higher average return in a backtest
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Does Scaling-in Work?' (Schoenberg and Corwin, 2010)
notes: V8 rule of thumb: mean-reversion experts enter all-in at one z-score level, no pyramiding; position_scaling variants should be added only if a frozen-OOS comparison beats the all-in baseline.
book: Algorithmic Trading - Winning Strategies and Their Rationale 2013

strategy_name: ATR trailing stop replacing the hard structural stop
mechanism: a volatility-scaled trailing stop protects open profit while giving the trade enough room to breathe through normal noise
setup_summary: On entry, the hard stop is a structural extreme (Y-day low for longs). Once the trade moves in favor, switch to an ATR-based trailing stop (author prefers 39-period ATR on daily bars) placed a multiple of ATR from price that only moves in the trade's favor; hold the hard stop until the ATR stop is tighter. Trade ends when either stop is touched.
trigger_invalidation: Exit only via the hard or trailing stop — the book explicitly accepts never exiting at highs/lows ('Only liars get out at the highs or lows').
risk_geometry: Entry + initial stop structural (channel/swing extreme); trailing exit = multiple of 39-period ATR from price, ratcheting in favor; no profit target.
quote: the ATR trailing stop is one way to limit losses and protect profits.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Stops' / 'If the Trade Starts Working' (True Range definition)
notes: Maps directly to V8 risk_geometry's atr_ref, adding the explicit rule: switch from structural hard stop to ATR trailing stop only once the ATR stop is tighter than the hard stop. The book's own trading-plan question (touch vs close-through on the ATR stop) is exactly the kind of frozen decision V8 requires. No gaps in crypto make the trailing stop precise; funding adds carry that must be absorbed by the ATR multiple.
book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

strategy_name: Trailing ATR stop as the single exit (Wilder ATR)
setup_summary: Every trade -- long or short, winner or loser -- is exited by the same trailing average-true-range stop, placed immediately on entry and honored the moment it is touched. The stop must be wide enough to let a working trend run (months-long holds are common) and tight enough to keep losses small (typical journal losses 0.2-1.2%). Falsifiable: exit exactly when price touches the trailing ATR stop; no discretionary exit, no 'it will come back' override.
trigger_invalidation: Exit trigger: price closes/prints at or beyond the trailing ATR stop. Invalidation of the trade thesis also occurs when the stop is hit -- stops and dead-thesis are the same exit here.
risk_geometry: Stop = trailing Wilder ATR multiple; target = none (no fixed R target; winners ride until stop); expiry = none (holds run 2 weeks to 5 months in journal); the 'two stops' are protective stops placed immediately upon entry.
quote: My trailing stop has protected me when trades have not worked, and when trades do work the trailing stop gives them enough room to run.
chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.169 (cotton exit); ATR calc ref pp.102-104
notes: Corroborates V8's existing use of atr_ref in trend_pullback/failed_breakout and the distinction between stops and dead-thesis exits. Journal confirms trailing ATR is applied identically on wins and losses (gold, cotton, silver, S&P, yen). In 24/7 perp trading the trailing stop is naturally executable at any hour; funding does not alter ATR-based stops.
book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

strategy_name: Carry trade on interest-rate differential
mechanism: Long the high-yield currency / short the low-yield funding currency to capture the interest-rate spread; trade only while realized volatility is low and the rate differential is wide
setup_summary: On a perp, identify the funding-rate analogue of the interest differential: when the (annualized) funding rate is persistently positive AND realized volatility is low, hold a SHORT perp to harvest positive funding while price stays range-bound; the book's formulation is 'identify a currency pair with a broad interest rate differential and low volatility, sit back, and start collecting interest.' Falsifiable: positive expectancy = funding accrual minus adverse price drift over the hold window, gated on a low-volatility regime.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: wide rate/funding differential + low volatility. Invalidation: sudden volatility spike or differential narrowing forces unwind; risk-appetite collapse causes a violent short squeeze in the funding leg (documented yen +25% in 2007-08).
risk_geometry: Entry: time-based (hold to accrue funding/interest), no price trigger; stop: volatility spike or differential narrowing (e.g., funding flips sign); target: accrual over horizon; expiry: funding normalizes. Exit discipline is regime-triggered, not price-triggered.
quote: the carry trade has become one of the most reliable trades in forex... the carry trade tends to thrive when volatility is low and to shrink during crises when uncertainty is high.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Carry Trade' pp.181-183; Ch.5 'Interest Rate Analysis' pp.96-98
notes: On USDM perps the interest differential is replaced by the funding rate paid between longs and shorts, so the trade is short-perp-when-funding-positive / long-perp-when-funding-negative. Book documents empirical carry returns Aug 2007-Jan 2012 (Figure 7-7) and the yen carry unwind (+25% in the funding leg). DATA_BLOCKED until funding-rate tape exists; this is the V8 'funding_carry' backlog family.
book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

strategy_name: N-based volatility-normalized unit sizing (1% equity per unit)
setup_summary: Size 1 unit = 1% of account equity / (N x dollars-per-point), where N is the 20-day exponential moving average of true range (ATR). One unit therefore moves ~1% of equity per 1N, so a 2N stop risks exactly 2% of equity. This equalizes dollar risk across markets of different volatility, making diversified positions comparable bets. N and unit sizes were recomputed weekly.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — sizing rule, no entry thesis.
risk_geometry: Volatility-derived unit size with fixed risk-per-unit (1%); stop distance 2N implies 2% per-trade risk.
quote: The Turtles used a position sizing algorithm that was very advanced for its day because it normalized the dollar volatility of a position by adjusting the position size on the basis of the dollar volatility of the market.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Position Sizing' and 'Volatility: The Meaning of N', pp. 251-255
notes: With 25-125x perp leverage, %-equity volatility-normalized sizing is the critical control; V8's risk_geometry (atr_ref) can directly host this. The 'How much to buy or sell is the single most important aspect of trading' claim and the stated failure mode ('Most beginning traders risk far too much on each trade') are falsifiable design inputs for the RiskGate sizing rule.
book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

strategy_name: Turtle 2N stop with 1/2N unit-tightening; Whipsaw 1/2N-stop re-entry variant
setup_summary: Initial stop is 2N from entry (2% equity risk). Each 1/2N add raises all earlier units' stops by 1/2N so the entire position sits 2N below the newest unit's fill. Stops are pre-defined and nonnegotiable: if price trades through, exit every time. Alternative 'Whipsaw' variant: stop at 1/2N (0.5% risk) and re-enter a stopped unit if price returns to the original entry price — more trades, lower win rate, better profitability.
trigger_invalidation: Stop is a hard exit, not a thesis condition; Whipsaw explicitly re-enters after stop-out on return to entry price.
risk_geometry: Stop: 2N below entry (long) / above entry (short), tightened per add; Whipsaw: 1/2N stop + re-entry at entry. No target (targets are exits, see trailing_stop).
quote: Turtles' stops were set at 2N below the entry for long positions and 2N above the entry for short positions... [Whipsaw] the stops were placed at 1/2N for 1/2 percent account risk. If a particular unit was stopped out, the unit would be reentered if the market reached the original entry price.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Turtle Stops' and 'Alternative Stop Strategy: The Whipsaw', pp. 262-266
notes: N-scaled stop placement (volatility-adaptive, equalized risk) is a direct input to V8 risk_geometry. The book's caveat that moving-average systems carry an implicit stop, while explicit stops matter psychologically, maps to V8's separation of stop vs. dead-thesis exits. Whipsaw re-entry (stop then re-enter at entry) is a distinct, testable exit/re-entry behavior. Perp note: no overnight gap risk, but liquidation cascades can trade through stops fast.
book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

strategy_name: Volatility-calibrated stop distance (stop outside normal noise)
setup_summary: Set stop distance so it exceeds the pair's normal fluctuation range to avoid premature stop-outs: USD/CAD weekly volatility averaged ~100 PIPs (1%) and never exceeded 135 PIPs, so a 100-PIP stop sits inside ordinary noise and 'could automatically lead to your position being closed before the pair has a chance to rebound.' Same data used to gauge worst-case exposure of a planned hold (3-week hold ~= 200 PIPs of risk).
trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - calibration guideline; the rule is that stops inside the realized-vol range trigger on noise, not on thesis death.
risk_geometry: stop_distance >= typical range for the hold horizon (e.g. >100 PIPs for USD/CAD at ~1% weekly vol); exposure budget = recent realized vol x hold-period factor.
quote: a fluctuation in the USD/CAD of 100 PIPs would hardly be considered exceptional, and placing a stop-loss at this level could automatically lead to your position being closed before the pair has a chance to rebound.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Volatility (Figure 10-2, USD/CAD volatility chart)
notes: Validates V8's atr_ref convention (stop distance in ATR multiples) and the separation of stops from dead-thesis exits: a stop inside normal noise exits for the wrong reason. Especially relevant on perps where leverage exaggerates noise around the stop.
book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

strategy_name: Volatility-normalized unit sizing (N / ATR = 1% of equity)
mechanism: Sizing every market so that one ATR of adverse movement equals a fixed fraction of equity equalizes per-trade dollar risk across instruments and, critically, equalizes exposure to price shocks regardless of stop distance
setup_summary: Unit size = (1% of account) / (dollar value of 1 ATR per contract). For a $1M account, 1-ATR = $10,000, so units in each market are chosen so daily fluctuations are approximately equal in dollars. The book's evidence: on the Oct 1987 shock, Curtis (1/2-ATR stop) would have lost 4x more if sized by stop-distance alone; volatility-based sizing gave all Turtles identical shock exposure.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a sizing rule, recomputed each day from the ATR (N) at entry.
risk_geometry: Sizing rule, not entry geometry; pairs with the 2N stop so each unit risks 1% of equity and max 4 units = 4% per market.
quote: Each unit was sized by determining the number of contracts where 1-ATR of price movement would be equal to 1 percent of our account size.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Risk and Money Management, The N Factor (pp.117-120); Ch.3 (pp.32-33)
notes: This is exactly V8's atr_ref/risk normalization principle already in the frozen spec (trend_pullback stop_r 1.0, atr_ref). The book adds two refinements: (a) size by ATR, not by stop distance - stop distance and exposure are decoupled (the 1/2-ATR vs 2-ATR stop story); (b) sizing must be re-frozen at entry and PIT - the 'number of contracts per million' was updated weekly. In perps, position sizing by ATR of the perp is direct since contract value = price x notional.
book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

strategy_name: ATR-relative position sizing (Size Ratio)
mechanism: sizing position size and stop distance as a function of volatility relative to price keeps per-trade dollar risk constant across instruments
setup_summary: Size Ratio = 10-day average close / 50-day ATR. Baseline exposure (e.g. 5% of capital); if Ratio < 50, cut position size 25% and widen the protective stop 25%; if Ratio > 75, raise size 25% and tighten the stop 25%.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (sizing rule, not an entry signal).
risk_geometry: Stop distance scaled inversely with the Size Ratio so net dollar risk stays constant per trade.
quote: Average closing price of last 10 days / 50-day ATR = Size Ratio
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Position Sizing'
notes: Author is explicit these are experience-derived guidelines, 'not derived from any high-tech mathematical algorithm'. Directly transferable to perp volatility targeting.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Sell-the-rich-side volatility skew structuring
mechanism: when implied volatilities differ across strikes, express a directional/neutral view by selling the high-IV leg and buying the low-IV leg
setup_summary: Feature/structuring rule: implied volatilities differ by strike (the skew/'smirk'/'smile'), with lower-strike options typically at higher IV. When the skew is steep, a bullish trader can make a reverse-collar more attractive because the put being sold carries much higher IV than the call being bought - selling the rich leg and buying the cheap leg adds a structuring 'edge'. A flat skew can make the bearish collar attractive for the same reason. The differential alone is never a sufficient reason to trade.
trigger_invalidation: A skew differential only structures a trade that already has a directional or range forecast; a differential without a market view is insufficient. Trade only when both conditions hold.
risk_geometry: Sell the high-IV side, buy the low-IV side; standard stop-loss discipline on the short leg at key levels.
quote: If the market demonstrates a large implied volatility skew, sometimes a reverse-collar trade becomes more appetizing to the bullish trader because the implied volatility of the put option being sold could be much higher than the implied volatility of the call option being bought, giving the trader an additional 'edge' to work with.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Collars and Reverse-Collars', 'Implied Volatility Skew' (p. 84)
notes: Perps have no options IV, so the direct analog is funding-rate asymmetry / skew (enter the side that receives funding when funding is extreme) - candidate input for a funding-skew feature and for structuring direction on funding-rich sides. Chapter 7 repeats the principle for ratio spreads as 'buy-low-volatility-strike, sell-high-volatility-strike' skew plays.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Volatility term-structure regime (short-dated spikes, long-dated tracks history)
mechanism: short-dated implied volatility spikes on volatile periods and collapses on quiet periods while long-dated IV tracks historical volatility, creating a term-structure shape that selects long vs short time-spread strategies
setup_summary: Feature input: implied volatility levels generally differ across expiration cycles (the term structure). After a slow period, near-term IV is depressed relative to long-dated (upward slope) - favoring short time spreads (sell the rich far-dated); after a volatile period, near-term IV is elevated (downward slope) - favoring long time spreads (buy the cheaper far-dated, sell the rich near-dated). The term structure must align with a price/time forecast; it is not sufficient to justify a trade on its own.
trigger_invalidation: Term structure must align with a price/time forecast to warrant a trade; a pure term-structure signal is insufficient (corroborates the 'yield is a trap' lesson).
risk_geometry: Long time spread: buy far-dated, sell near-dated at target strike; positive theta + long vega, risk limited to debit; short time spread is the reverse (positive gamma, short vega) but carries unquantifiable short-side risk through the near expiry.
quote: The implied volatility of short-dated options will conform to short-term events, spiking when underlying price movement is volatile, collapsing when it is not, whereas the longer-dated options will trade more in line with the historical long-term volatility.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'Calendar Spreads', 'Implied Volatility Differentials' (p. 174)
notes: For perps the analog is short-window vs long-window realized-volatility divergence plus the funding-rate term structure - a regime classifier input for gating volatility-sensitive families (e.g., run mean-reversion/range trades in the collapsed-vol regime, favor expansion plays after vol compression).
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: 2N ATR Hard Stop (touch-based exit)
mechanism: Sizing the stop to 2× daily volatility normalizes loss across markets and regimes so a stop-out costs roughly the same amount of risk every time.
setup_summary: Place the primary hard stop at entry ± 2N, where N = 20-day average of true range (max of high-low, |high-prev close|, |low-prev close|). Exit when the stop price is touched — no second-guessing, no bar-close confirmation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades through the 2N stop level. Invalidated: none — the stop is unconditional and mechanical.
risk_geometry: Entry-dependent stop distance = 2N (2×ATR) behind entry; STOP_FIRST touch semantics (matches V8 simulator); combined with the opposite-channel breakout as the second exit, whichever hits first.
quote: The Turtles used a 2N stop. This simply means that their primary stop, or hard stop, was two times the daily 'N.' ... You would exit if the stop at price level $236 was 'touched.' No second-guessing. No overthinking. Follow the rules.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', Risk Management (p. 84)
notes: Refines existing V8 stop conventions (current experts use stop_r 1.0 with atr_ref): Turtle used 2×ATR and touch-based exit. Directly implementable as a RiskGate/risk_geometry rule; ATR (N) already exists in the volatility feature group.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Money Abstraction and Memoryless Trading (N-units not dollars)
mechanism: Anchoring to dollars, past entry prices, or prior equity distorts decisions; trading in volatility units (N) and treating equity as a current-state variable keeps the trader on the rules.
setup_summary: Rule-adherence doctrine: think 'I have a half-unit on' not '$34M in bonds'; risk 2% of CURRENT equity (never of peak or original); never average down on a losing position ('adding to a loser is putting your hand back on the stove'); re-enter after a stop-out if the signal re-fires (Paul Tudor Jones re-entered 10 times before the trend paid).
trigger_invalidation: Not a tradable rule — a determinism/psychology guardrail. Violations (discretionary adds, vendetta re-entry in the same losing market, averaging down) are the behaviors V8's mechanical pipeline eliminates by construction.
risk_geometry: None — behavioral constraint; operationalized in V8 as no wall-clock dependence, frozen refs, and dead-thesis (still_valid) exits.
quote: You shouldn't care about how you got to the current state but rather about what you should do now. A trader who trades differentially because of swings in confidence is focusing on his or her own past rather than on current realities.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'The Philosophy' (p. 58); losses/vendetta (pp. 60-62)
notes: The behavioral failure modes the Turtles were trained against (averaging down, revenge re-entry, entry-price anchoring, funny-money on profits) are exactly the discretionary risks V8 removes via deterministic rules, frozen refs, and single-exposure lifecycle. Also: the discretionary S3 'flair account' was canned within ~6 weeks — supportive evidence for REJECT_FOR_V8 on discretionary sub-accounts.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: ATR-unit fixed-fractional sizing with disciplined leverage cap
mechanism: Position size is set so each unit risks a fixed fraction of equity (scaled by ATR/N) and total portfolio leverage is capped so survival outranks return maximization.
setup_summary: Size each trade so risk equals a fixed fraction of equity (one unit ~ 1% of equity per N); when drawdowns or volatility demand it, cut gross leverage (Dennis's 50% leverage-cut memo and Crocker's 'back off the leverage' both assert this). Abraham's rule of thumb: 'never going past 30' even though the vehicle allows 160.
trigger_invalidation: Standing rule, not a trade setup; governs all positions continuously.
risk_geometry: Book (this part) asserts the leverage-cap principle; stop = 2N from entry and unit = 1%-of-equity-per-N are Part 1 details. V8: map to RiskGate admission + heat cap.
quote: If you make 30 percent a year, people will beat a path to your door. You need to back off on the leverage.
chapter_anchor: Ch.13, Commodities Corporation meeting (p.182); leverage memo referenced in Ch.14 (p.188)
notes: With perp leverage up to 100x, ATR-based fractional sizing is the primary risk control; the leverage-reduction-on-stress rule is a lifecycle signal (cut heat, not the system).
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Distinguish volatility from risk (tail blowups hide under low vol)
mechanism: tail_risk_measurement: using volatility/standard deviation as the risk measure misprices strategies whose real risk is a rare catastrophic tail; 'works 95% of the time' strategies are exactly the ones that blow up.
setup_summary: When evaluating any candidate (strategy, expert, or portfolio), measure risk by drawdown path and fat-tail/liquidation exposure, not by vol alone; reject candidates whose 95% window hides a ruin tail.
trigger_invalidation: Evaluation principle, not a trade setup.
risk_geometry: None stated; the point is that vol-based risk geometry misprices tail risk.
quote: The biggest single problem with these allocators is they completely confuse volatility and standard deviation with 'risk.' The two are completely noncorrelated. They want Amaranth, Long Term Capital Management . . . and that's going to work 95 percent of the time, but when it doesn't, they're broke.
chapter_anchor: Appendix I, Jim DiMaria (pp.192-193)
notes: Guidance for V8 registry gates and OOS evaluation: report tail metrics (max DD, liquidation-path stress), not only mean/variance, when screening challengers.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Event pre-pricing / post-event volatility crush
mechanism: Anticipated scheduled events are pre-priced into volatility; once the event resolves, volatility crushes — a position can be right about direction yet lose because the pre-paid premium collapses.
setup_summary: Methodology lesson with a falsifiable perp analog: entering a breakout/momentum position immediately before a scheduled high-impact event (macro releases, liquidations) carries negative expected edge because the move is pre-priced and realized volatility mean-reverts after the event. Test: compare forward returns/vol of entries taken before vs. after scheduled events on BTC.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — methodology lesson, not an executable setup. The scenario: correct 20-point move, long-straddle still only +1 because IV collapsed after the announcement.
risk_geometry: N/A
quote: Even though the movement that was anticipated occurred, the volatility was crushed and the position made very little money.
chapter_anchor: Appendix, Final Exam Part II, Scenario 4, p. 261
notes: No IV surface on perps, but the analog — realized-vol and funding dynamics around scheduled events, and the general point that event positioning is crowded — informs V8's regime filter and event-timing feature work. Presented as practitioner market behavior in a worked exam, no statistics.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Commercial Net Position Climax Contrarian Signal
mechanism: commercials (hedgers) are structurally contrarian; when their net position reaches a historical climax the market is near a major turn
setup_summary: On the weekly COT release, rank the commercial net position against its multi-year look-back range (COT Index, stochastic formula). A buying climax (index >= 90) or selling climax (index <= 5), confirmed when the index backs off the extreme, marks a major turn; take the commercial side (buy climax -> long, sell climax -> short). NASDAQ selling climax Oct 8 2007 flagged the stock-index top ~3 days before it, and the author carried 13 consecutive weekly warnings before the January 2008 break.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: index backs off the extreme (confirmation). Invalidation: index holds at the extreme while price continues — major sell signals can be premature inside bull trends (e.g., Nov 2004), so the claim is a success-ratio edge, not a certainty.
risk_geometry: Entry on the next weekly open after the COT release applying the correct release lag; the book's Part 2 gives no stop/target — V8 must assign atr_ref stop, 1R target, expiry in bars.
quote: Commercial selling reported in last Tuesday's Commitments report triggered a major COT sell signal in the NASDAQ.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'COT Signals Stock Market Top' (Fig. E.1); Glossary 'climax'
notes: No CFTC COT per-type breakdown exists for most perp venues (only CME BTC/ETH futures have COT). Funding rate and open interest can proxy for the positioning gauge but lack trader-type labels and are real-time, which removes the stale-data edge the book exploits.
book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

strategy_name: Failed COT Signal Explosive Counter-Move
mechanism: when commercials fail to defend a level after their positioning climaxed against a direction, the unresolved positioning unwinds explosively in the opposite direction
setup_summary: After a COT sell (buy) signal, if price does not decline (rise) and instead closes back through the level commercials were defending, expect an explosive move in the opposite direction. Gold 2007: a successful commercial selling climax in July was followed in September by the failure of commercials to hold resistance at the same price level (a 'COT sell signal failure'), and the ensuing move pushed gold to record highs.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back through the failed level after a positioning climax. Invalidation: the original signal resolves in its own direction (price keeps declining after a sell signal).
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE beyond the failed level; stop on the far side of the failed level; target is trend-following (ride the explosive move); no explicit R-multiple stated.
quote: the failure of commercials to hold resistance at the same price level in September created a COT sell signal failure (point C). Following typical form, the ensuing move was quite explosive, pushing gold prices to record levels.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'Gold Responds to COT Buy Signal' (Fig. E.2)
notes: Single-case pattern in this part; 'typical form' implies repetition but only one example is shown here. Conceptually adjacent to V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim / failed_breakout dynamics but conditioned on a positioning-climax signal.
book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

strategy_name: Worst-case planning with fixed fractional risk
mechanism: constant percentage risk per trade normalizes equity volatility across trades and builds position-size discipline (trading tolerance)
setup_summary: Size every position so the dollar loss if the stop is hit equals the same fixed percentage of account (1-2%). Compute worst case = dollar loss at the stop, add 20% buffer, and assume that amount of risk for every trade. This keeps the emotional amplitude of any single trade constant so execution quality stays stable.
trigger_invalidation: n/a (sizing rule, not an entry trigger)
risk_geometry: position size = (risk% x equity) / (stop distance + ~20% buffer)
quote: First, calculate your worst-case scenario. This should be the dollar loss if your stop loss is hit. Second, add 20 percent to this amount... assume this (percentage) risk for all of your trades.
chapter_anchor: Ch 16, Worst-Case Planning / Trading Tolerance (pp. 254-255)
notes: With 5-50x leverage available on perps, fixed-% risk sizing is the only sane default; ties position size to stop distance (V8's stop_distance_atr analog). The +20% buffer covers slippage/funding on high-volatility perps. The 'trading tolerance' psychological claim is not falsifiable; the sizing formula is.
book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

strategy_name: SIP-latency / stale-price arbitrage (public vs private quote feed)
mechanism: The public consolidated quote (SIP) lags private feeds built inside exchanges; fast traders buy at a stale public bid or sell at a stale public offer, and the value of the early view scales with volatility because volatility creates new prices to see first.
setup_summary: Trade the gap between the public consolidated quote (NBBO via the SIP) and a faster private feed: buy when the fast feed shows a higher price than the public bid, sell when it shows a lower price than the public offer. Edge per window scales with realized volatility and with the feed-latency gap (up to ~25ms in the book's example). Empirical anchor cited in the book: UC Berkeley researchers counted 55,000 SIP-vs-fast-feed price divergences for Apple in a single day, each a potential stale-price exploitation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence between public and private feed prices exceeding the latency*volatility product. Thesis (stale prices are exploitable by speed) invalidates if the latency advantage yields no consistent positive fill differential, or once the SIP is modernized to private-feed speed.
risk_geometry: No stop/target stated; per-window arbitrage with inventory and latency as binding constraints; not executable at bar-close frequency.
quote: That's why volatility was so valuable to high-frequency traders: It created new prices for fast traders to see first and to exploit.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 (Tracking the Predator) - Reg NMS / SIP loophole and the UC Berkeley 2013 study
notes: Falsifiable empirical case (cited 2013 UC Berkeley study with a concrete daily divergence count) for an intra-millisecond latency strategy. Not executable on BTCUSDT 1h bars or on a single-venue bar tape; retained only as market-structure context (why microstructure edges are speed- and volatility-dependent, and why 'public' aggregated feeds can lag reality).
book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

strategy_name: Risk as thesis failure, not price volatility
mechanism: Risk is the possibility of harm from misjudging the value/thesis, not the volatility of the price; a price dip on an intact thesis reduces risk
setup_summary: Risk-definition lesson: 'the academics' definition of risk' (volatility) is rejected; risk = possibility of harm, a function of misjudging the business/thesis plus uncontrollable effects. For V8: thesis-failure risk should govern invalidation, and volatility should not be the sole basis for risk gating or sizing.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (risk-definition framework).
risk_geometry: N/A; conceptual. ATR-based stops remain execution tools, not the definition of risk.
quote: Buffett has a different definition of risk: the possibility of harm. And that is a factor of the intrinsic value of the business, not the price behavior of the stock.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10 Managing Your Portfolio (Buffett's View of Risk), pp. 165
notes: Cautions against vol-normalized sizing or vol-only gating as the risk model: the operative risk in V8 is dead-thesis (still_valid) persistence. In perps the thesis anchor is thin (no intrinsic value), so thesis-failure risk concentrates in event/liquidity risk, which supports the existing regime and liquidation-aware risk rules.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Leverage to drawdown tolerance, not margin adequacy
mechanism: Exchange margin is a lagging indicator of risk - raised only after volatility has already hurt the account; sizing should target a maximum drawdown the trader can sustain, because fully-leveraged positions can lose more than account equity.
setup_summary: Fully-margined commodity positions can wipe an account: with $1,000 equity controlling two fully-margined corn contracts, a $0.15 adverse move turns the account into a $500 debit. Experienced traders ignore margin and size by fixed-risk percent so expected max DD stays inside personal tolerance; risked-per-trade 0.25%->1% scales max DD 11.8%->37.4% (Ch.14 Table 14.10). The book's cautions: only a small fraction of traders can sit through a 40-50% drawdown, and margin changes always arrive after the volatility.
trigger_invalidation: In high-leverage perps, liquidation and funding make the book's 'many adverse trades from a margin call' buffer much thinner; a sizing rule anchored only to margin/liquidation distance is insufficient - it must be anchored to a tolerable max-DD percentile.
risk_geometry: leverage multiplier scaled to DD tolerance; fixed-risk percent x equity / stop distance defines size.
quote: Most experienced commodity traders don't even consider margin requirements when trading. Their money management considers risk from a draw-down probability standpoint, and they leverage to experience draw-downs within their personal risk tolerance, not to margin requirements... Margin requirements are no help because they are a lagging indicator of risk.
chapter_anchor: Appendix B 'Margin', pp. 262-263; Ch.14 Table 14.10, p. 230
notes: Perps offer 20-125x leverage with instantaneous liquidation and deleveraging cascades, so anchoring risk sizing to a sustainable max-DD budget (per-trade risk fraction + heat cap) rather than liquidation distance is directly actionable and consistent with V8's deterministic RiskGate and NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM stance.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Loss-based risk measurement
mechanism: risk is the possibility of loss, not price volatility; volatility/beta-style measures mis-rank assets and mis-measure strategy risk
setup_summary: Methodology rule: V8 risk evaluation must use loss-based quantities (per-episode drawdown, probability of hitting stop, expected adverse excursion) rather than price volatility as the primary risk metric. A strategy that lost money is 'riskier' at the lower equity level, not safer; beta-like metrics cannot distinguish a structurally declining asset from a stable one.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (methodology).
risk_geometry: Risk gates expressed in R-units and drawdown, not vol-normalized metrics; stops and dead-thesis exits remain the risk surface.
quote: It is better to be approximately right than precisely wrong.
chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1993), pp. 75-77; 'equating beta with investment risk makes no sense' p. 78
notes: Perp crypto is high-vol by construction; vol-based risk measures would drown in noise. Loss/ruin framing matches V8's stop, dead-thesis (still_valid) and per-episode R accounting.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Volatility-scaled catastrophic stop, triggered on close with next-open exit
mechanism: trade risk should scale with recent volatility because dollar stops are simultaneously too tight for volatile instruments and too loose for quiet ones; a stop is a risk-control measure, not a profit enhancer
setup_summary: Place the catastrophic stop at 3x the 20-day standard deviation of closes from entry (best variant; dollar stops, Donchian-midpoint stops, and average-range stops all underperformed it). If the stop level is breached on a close, exit at the next open - the book shows next-open exit beats intraday resting-stop exit.
trigger_invalidation: Stop trigger: close through the 3-SD level. Thesis: stops cap drawdown but systematically lower profit-per-trade; they should be adopted on risk grounds only.
risk_geometry: Entry-price +/- 3 x 20-day SD of closes; triggered on close, executed next open; the book's repeated finding is 'a stop loss doesn't increase your total profit' yet cuts max drawdown - accept the profit-per-trade tax.
quote: the best risk/reward solution usually lies with a stop executed at either the close or the next open
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Exit Stops (Stock Example)
notes: Corroborates V8's atr_ref stop geometry. The next-open execution finding matters for crypto: 24/7 markets mean resting stops DO fill (unlike overnight commodity sessions), but liquidation-engine wicks and stop-runs argue for the same close-triggered/next-bar-open execution to avoid wick fills. V8's STOP_FIRST simulator already encodes order priority; this book's evidence justifies the close-trigger/next-open execution path.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Balance/imbalance phase regime (fast follows slow)
mechanism: balance leads to imbalance: horizontal low-volatility phases and vertical high-volatility phases alternate, so the end of a slow phase precedes the next directional move; the two phases are mutually exclusive and are traded differently
setup_summary: Classify each BTCUSDT 1h window as horizontal (balanced: narrow range, overlapping bars, fat volume-at-price profile) or vertical (imbalanced: wide non-overlapping bars, skinny profile). Trade only the vertical phase; enter directional trades as horizontal ends (profile transitions fat->skinny) and prefer trading the fast-to-slow side; stand aside when slow becomes slower (fat->fatter profiles, 'multiple consecutively slower and slower profiles often lead to very fast vertical moves').
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: profile shape transition fat->skinny after a slow phase, or price exiting the value area with non-overlapping bars. Invalidation: price re-enters balance without directional follow-through (fast probe fails quickly, e.g. V-pivot); correct phase identification is the whole premise, so the phase classifier itself must be falsified on frozen OOS.
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close of the directional break out of balance; stop beyond the balance extreme or probe extreme; target at the next horizontal-development area (far side of the move); the chapter demands >=4:1 reward-to-risk for any trade taken in the phase.
quote: Fast vertical market movements follow slow horizontal market movements. This is an either/or state.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 222-240) 'Balance versus Imbalance' / Figures 5.4-5.9, 'Relative Balance Leads to Relative Imbalance'
notes: The 24/7 perp tape has no opening gaps, so profile/horizontal-development continuity is cleaner than in index futures, making the fat/skinny profile classifier computable from 1h bars + volume-at-price. Maps to a marketstate regime feature (horizontal vs vertical phase + maturity) that gates trend_pullback/breakout families; the fast-to-slow position guidance (stay while profiles skinny, tighten stops while fatter) is a lifecycle management companion.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Contrarian sentiment extremes (bullish consensus / VIX / put-call / COT -> funding + positioning for perps)
mechanism: when positioning is one-sided at an extreme, the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted and price is vulnerable to reversal; volatility and fear gauges are contrarian - extreme complacency marks tops, extreme fear marks bottoms
setup_summary: Bullish consensus near 75-85% after a prolonged uptrend, or a low fear/volatility gauge while price is at highs, or extremely one-sided positioning (COT: small specs extreme one way, commercials/large specs opposite at an extreme price) -> anticipate a correction. Extreme put-to-call readings signal bottoms; extreme low readings signal tops. Crypto analogs: funding rate at sustained extremes, extreme long/short positioning, high perp OI at highs, margin-requirement changes. Always confirm with price action before fading.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sentiment gauge reaches its historical extreme band while price sits at a corresponding price extreme. Thesis invalidation: sentiment stays extreme and price keeps trending (extremes persist in leverage-driven markets); the book itself warns 'never get bearish in the hole' and that a low VIX does not always mean price will drop (volatility can rise from rallies).
risk_geometry: entry only after price confirmation (candle/pivot signal) since sentiment alone is timing-weak; stop beyond the swing extreme; target = prior support/mean or pivot level; expiry = swing.
quote: The bottom line: When everyone is bullish, don't join them... 'Buy it when nobody wants it, and sell it when everybody has got to have it.'
chapter_anchor: Ch 9, 'Market Vane', 'Commitments of Traders', 'Put-to-Call Ratio', 'VIX', 'Summary'
notes: Perp crypto has real-time funding rate, OI and long/short ratios - closer analogs to COT/VIX than equity data. But positioning data persists extreme in strong trends and perp leverage makes contrarian timing expensive; the book's own caveats (media lag: 'by the time it gets on the news, the move is probably over') support using this as a regime/confirmation overlay rather than a standalone entry.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Volatility Is Not Risk (risk is probability of permanent loss, not price variance)
mechanism: risk is the probability of permanent loss of capital, not the size of price jiggles; measuring risk by beta/volatility misprices lumpy opportunities and teaches the wrong stop behavior
setup_summary: 'Volatility is no measure of risk to us' - Buffett buys farmland after a 70% price collapse (which beta theory would call maximally risky) and writes supercat insurance that loses in a given year but wins over a decade; a lumpy 20-80% return is not riskier than a smooth 5%. Real risk is the nature of the economics and 'not knowing what you're doing' - the probability and size of thesis failure, not variance. For V8: risk gates should be driven by scenario loss of capital (thesis death, liquidation) rather than by volatility alone; volatility may size a position but should not be the definition of risk.
trigger_invalidation: Standing philosophy; it binds when risk measures and stop sizing are designed.
risk_geometry: Size by worst-case scenario loss of principal, not by volatility-scaled distance alone; a stop may be wide (structure-based) while the position remains small in scenario-loss terms.
quote: Volatility is no measure of risk to us.
chapter_anchor: 1994 'Modern Portfolio Theory Described'; 2007 'Comments on Risk'
notes: Design principle for the RiskGate: in perp crypto the true tail risk is liquidation and thesis death, not ATR-sized wiggles; V8 should separate volatility-based position sizing from permanent-loss-based risk admission.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

strategy_name: Fat-tailed returns and non-stationary volatility (critique of 'risk = historical volatility')
mechanism: Black-Scholes treated volatility as a constant, inherent trait and Merton assumed continuous time (no jumps); in reality returns are leptokurtic and markets gap, so any sizing, stop, or loss-odds estimate built from historical volatility systematically underprices tail losses.
setup_summary: Methodological constraint, not a trade setup: Fama's documented finding is that for individual stocks, a price move of more than 5 standard deviations should occur once per ~7,000 years under a normal distribution but in fact occurs about once every 3-4 years. Any V8 expert or RiskGate that converts realized/historical volatility into position size, stop distance (atr_stop), expiry, or 'loss odds' must be audited for fat tails; Black Monday (a 23% single-day drop, ~1-in-a-trillion under normality) is the canonical counterexample.
trigger_invalidation: n/a - the finding is that a 5+ sigma 1h-bar move is always in the near tail; a vol-derived sizing rule is invalidated whenever it assumes log-normality. Also 'markets have memories' (momentum/herding), so the i.i.d. random-walk premise fails.
risk_geometry: stop_distance_atr, expiry_bars, and leverage set from realized vol inherit the fat-tail error; tail-aware alternatives are robust quantiles of realized excursions rather than sigma multiples; LTCM's own disclosure ('lose at least 5% in 1 month in 5, 10%+ in 1 in 10, 20%+ only 1 year in 50') is precisely the miscalibration this finding warns about.
quote: more than five standard deviations from the mean should be observed about once every 7,000 years. In fact such observations seem to occur about once every three to four years.
chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Dear Investors', pp.61-74 (Fama's fat-tail thesis pp.70-72; Black Monday pp.68, 72-73)
notes: Crypto perps are more volatile and more leptokurtic than 1994 bond markets, and 24/7 trading with no price limits/auction halt means gap/overshoot risk materializes intra-bar. Also the book's volatility-targeting description (LTCM borrowed more when portfolio 'too quiet', reduced leverage when 'too volatile') shows vol-targeting was itself a mechanism, not just an estimate - but it rests on the same fragile vol estimate.
book: When Genius Failed - The Rise and Fall of Long-Term Capital Management 2001

strategy_name: Stop-loss failure taxonomy (whipsaw, slippage, fundamental shift) and ATR-based stop distance
mechanism: A stop converts to a market order on trigger, so it fills at the worst price in fast markets (slippage), gets whipsawed by tight placement in consolidation, and sits too far to survive fundamental supply/demand shifts
setup_summary: Classify every stop-based exit into one of three failure modes: (1) fast-moving market - triggered stop becomes market order and fills with slippage; (2) consolidating market - stop too tight is hit then price resumes expected direction (whipsaw); (3) fundamental shift - stop placed wide to survive consolidation is blown through with oversized loss. Cited countermeasure: place stops at about 1.5x true range to avoid whipsaw.
trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - risk-design taxonomy.
risk_geometry: Stop distance floor ~1.5x true range (ATR) to reduce whipsaw; acknowledge slippage/gap risk inherent in stop-to-market conversion; stop and protective-exit are different exits (reactive vs proactive).
quote: Stops are not a risk management tool; they are a panic button to help you out when all else fails.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6 pp. 103-106; stop wisdom list p. 104
notes: Maps to V8's stop (RiskGate) vs dead-thesis/still_valid (lifecycle) distinction - the book's reactive-vs-proactive split is the same line V8 draws. Encode a stop-distance floor in risk_geometry and keep stop-to-market slippage realistic in src/v8/simulator.py; 24/7 perps have no daily gaps but liquidation cascades create gap-like jumps.
book: Trade Like a Pro - 15 High-Profit Trading Strategies 2009
